steps.label: What charging is
steps.margin_note: Definition with ATP and the alternative name. Six lines.
lines: CHARGING of tRNA is the ACTIVATION of an amino
acid, in the presence of ATP, and its linking to
A tRNA carrying its amino acid is a CHARGED tRNA,
steps.why: An amino acid on its own cannot recognise a codon, so it has to be attached to a tRNA that can — charging is what makes the amino acid readable.
common_mistakes: Saying charging means giving the tRNA an electrical charge. It means LOADING it with an amino acid.
Leaving out ATP. The activation step needs it.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.margin_note: Say what only a charged tRNA can do, and why the matching matters.

lines.text: Only a charged tRNA can add its amino acid

lines: Only a CHARGED tRNA can take part in translation.
An uncharged tRNA carries nothing to add to the
Charging is what matches each codon to the right
steps.why: The accuracy of the whole genetic code depends on each tRNA being loaded with the correct amino acid, so charging is where translation can go wrong.
common_mistakes: Giving only the definition. The significance is a whole mark.
Saying an uncharged tRNA still works. It cannot contribute to the chain.
steps.memory_tip: An empty tRNA has nothing to give.
